title: Supporting Large Capital Delivery
narrative: We require a project and programme management capability in the architecture, represented in the business and application domains. This is based on a requirement for the business to support Large Capital Project delivery going forward, enabling delivery both internally and through external vendors and suppliers.

architecture-review.finding: The BUS-CAP catalogue at architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/business/conceptual/BUS-CAP/BUS-CAP.json defines nine level-1 capabilities (CAP-001 through CAP-009). None represents Project and Programme Management. CAP-005 (Asset Management) includes CAP-005-02 Acquire and Construct Assets, which touches capital delivery only incidentally, and CAP-009 (Enterprise Support) covers corporate services generically. Neither provides an anchor for programme governance, capital project lifecycle, or vendor-managed delivery.
architecture-review.impact: The narrative explicitly requires a project and programme management capability in the business domain. Without a dedicated level-1 entry in BUS-CAP, no downstream artefact — BUS-PRO processes, BUS-PRN principles, or APP-DAP platform mappings — can be correctly traced to a declared business capability. Any future strategy-alignment or capability-to-application mapping check will fail for this change.
architecture-review.recommendation: Add a new level-1 capability CAP-010 Project and Programme Management to architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/business/conceptual/BUS-CAP/BUS-CAP.json with importance set to strategic. Add at least three level-2 sub-capabilities under it: CAP-010-01 Portfolio and Programme Governance, CAP-010-02 Capital Project Delivery, and CAP-010-03 Project Controls and Reporting. CAP-010-02 should explicitly reference both internal and vendor/supplier delivery modes to reflect the narrative requirement.
architecture-review.rationale: BUS-CAP is the authoritative business capability register for this client version. Registering a new top-level capability before any dependent artefacts are authored ensures that all downstream work in the business, application, and data domains can be coherently traced back to a single, versioned anchor.

architecture-review.finding: The APP-DAP catalogue at architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/application/logical/APP-DAP/APP-DAP.json contains no platform for end-to-end project or programme management. PLAT-ERP (APP-DOM-ENTERPRISE) covers finance, procurement, and project accounting but does not represent a PPM or project scheduling tool. No other platform in the catalogue addresses project planning, resource management, programme governance, or vendor/contractor coordination.
architecture-review.impact: Without a PPM platform entry in APP-DAP, the application layer has no support for the capability being introduced in BUS-CAP. The proposed change requires the business to deliver large capital projects both internally and through external vendors; neither delivery mode is reflected in the current application catalogue. Capability-to-application traceability cannot be established, and the application domain remains incomplete at the logical layer.
architecture-review.recommendation: Add a new platform entry PLAT-PPM Project and Programme Management to APP-DAP/APP-DAP.json, associated with APP-DOM-ENTERPRISE (consistent with the existing enterprise support domain boundary). The description should cover project scheduling, resource and capacity management, programme governance, and integration with PLAT-ERP for project accounting and cost management. Assign a lifecycle value of trial if no tool has been adopted yet, or adopt if one is already in use.
architecture-review.rationale: APP-DAP is the single catalogue of logical application platforms for this client version. Introducing a business capability without a corresponding application platform creates a gap at the logical layer that cannot be resolved at the physical or solution layers without first being declared here.

architecture-review.finding: The BUS-PRO catalogue at architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/business/conceptual/BUS-PRO/BUS-PRO.json is currently empty (processes array is []). The narrative introduces a project and programme management capability that will require business processes to be defined — at minimum covering capital project initiation, delivery governance, and vendor management.
architecture-review.impact: An empty BUS-PRO catalogue is acceptable as a starting state, but once CAP-010 is added to BUS-CAP, the absence of corresponding BUS-PRO entries will leave the conceptual business domain incomplete. Process-level analysis and capability-to-process mapping will not be possible until processes are defined.
architecture-review.recommendation: After adding CAP-010 to BUS-CAP, add at least three process entries to BUS-PRO/BUS-PRO.json aligned to the new capability: capital project initiation and approval, capital project delivery and controls, and vendor and supplier management. This work can follow in a subsequent ADR or as part of this one.
architecture-review.rationale: BUS-PRO and BUS-CAP are both conceptual business-domain catalogues; completeness at the conceptual layer requires both capabilities and their supporting processes to be declared. Noting the gap now ensures it is tracked and not overlooked when the application and integration domains are subsequently populated.

architecture-review.finding: No new artefact types need to be created to represent this change. BUS-CAP, BUS-PRO, and APP-DAP are all existing, schema-backed catalogue types that cover the required content. The artefact-type registry in documentation/artefacts.md does not need modification.
architecture-review.impact: Confining the change to instance data in existing artefact types avoids the overhead of schema authoring, schema documentation, artefact-type registry updates, and new folder creation that would be required if a new artefact type were introduced.
architecture-review.recommendation: Proceed by updating instance files only: architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/business/conceptual/BUS-CAP/BUS-CAP.json, architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/business/conceptual/BUS-PRO/BUS-PRO.json, and architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/application/logical/APP-DAP/APP-DAP.json.
architecture-review.rationale: Reusing existing artefact types is the correct approach when the required content fits within already-defined schemas. New artefact types are only warranted when an entirely new output format or domain-layer combination is needed, which is not the case here.
